text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Somalia inquiry plans counterattack: Commissioners to delay report's submission until last minute to block Ottawa from minimizing impact.
- Euphoria, nostalgia mark end of empire: Hong Kong tinged with worry.
- UI surplus a quandary for Liberals: Account brings in an embarassing C$5 billion a year more than it pays out.
- Summer a wee bit longer this year: One leap second keeps time in line.
- Family ties trip up would-be immigrant: Canada says applicant is member of American Cosa Nostra.
- Emotions mixed for handover: Chinese Canadians feel sense of pride.
- Rockwell wins huge Lear deal: Contract with automotive seat maker will mean 100 new jobs at Ontario plant.
- Foreign brokerages gain foothold: Winning a bigger share of lucrative Canadian mergers and acquisitions.

- Bulls dominate Hong Kong on eve of handover: But behind exuberance over the territory's return to China tomorrow are reservations about an overheated stock market, competitive pressures and increased corruption.
- Retail stocks a hot fashion but investor caution urged.
- Royal takes aim at insurance with C$2.4 billion London bid: Takeover would give the bank 3,500 trained sales people to take its products to Canada's 'kitchen tables.'
- Jean Monty named CEO of the year.
- Who will blink first in Southam standoff.
